transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. 

Um... well, I've just been struggling a little bit lately, I suppose. I usually try to just push through things and not be a bother, but... well, to be completely honest—and I feel a little embarrassed even saying this out loud, so please bear with me—what actually scared me enough to make the appointment is that I keep having these thoughts that it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. 

And... sometimes when I’m driving home from the veterinary clinic after my shift, I catch myself just wondering what would happen if I didn’t turn the wheel. I know that sounds awful, and I'm really sorry to drop something so heavy on you right away, but I figured that meant I should probably come in and talk to someone. I'm in the right place for that, aren't I?
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up or wondering what would happen if you didn't turn the wheel while driving?

Um... well, it hasn't been forever or anything like that, I promise. I really don't want to sound dramatic. I'd say it's been... maybe about a month? 

We, um... we recently had to take in a relative, and... well, it's just been this really intense up-and-down crisis around that whole situation. I feel terrible even calling it a crisis, honestly, because I know I should just be strong and be glad I can help family, but it's just been a really overwhelming four weeks or so. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this okay.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do over the past month?

Um... well, I try to keep up with everything, I really do. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I feel a bit guilty even admitting this—I haven't really been enjoying much of anything lately. 

I usually love being outside, but... I haven't touched my camera in weeks. And the bird feeders... I usually keep such a close eye on them, but I just haven't checked them with any real interest at all. I haven't even cared what's coming up in the garden. 

It's actually a little frightening for me, because... well, doing those things, that's usually how I feel like myself. I just feel awful that I can't even muster up the energy to care about the things I love right now. I hope I don't sound like I'm just being lazy or whining to you... is it normal to just lose yourself like that when things get stressful?
Have you experienced a lack of pleasure in activities that you normally find enjoyable over the past month?

Oh, um... yes, exactly. I'm so sorry, did I not explain that very well a moment ago? I know I can ramble a bit when I'm nervous, please forgive me. 

But yes, that's exactly what it feels like—a complete lack of pleasure. Like I was just saying, I haven't touched my camera, and I haven't checked the bird feeders with any real interest... or even cared what's coming up in the garden. I really hate admitting it because it makes me sound so ungrateful for the nice things in my life. It's just frightening to me because doing those things... that used to be how I felt like myself. 

I'm so sorry to repeat myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or the way you move over the past month?

Um... well, I really try not to complain about being tired, because I know everyone gets tired, and I don't want to sound weak. But... yes, I suppose there has been a change. I just have almost no energy at all lately. 

I feel a bit guilty even saying it out loud, but at the clinic... just walking from the treatment area over to the lab benches, it honestly feels like I'm dragging myself through thick mud. I try so hard to hide it from the other techs so I'm not a burden to the team. But by the time I get home, I'm just... completely spent. I can barely even manage to make dinner or help out with the evening care routine for our relative. 

I know I should be doing more, and I feel awful that I can't seem to keep up right now. Does that answer your question? I really hope I don't just sound like I'm making excuses for being lazy...
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight over the past month?

Um... well, I haven't really been weighing myself, so I'm not entirely sure about the exact numbers. I know I should be paying better attention to that, I'm sorry. 

But... I suppose my appetite has been a bit all over the place. I really don't want to make a fuss about it, but lately, I find myself just picking at a piece of toast or maybe just having coffee in the morning. And then... well, I'll get to the end of a long shift at the clinic and realize I've barely eaten anything all day. 

I feel a bit silly admitting it, because I know how important it is to keep my strength up, especially with the animals and helping out at home. I just haven't had much of a taste for anything. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I can try to be more specific if you need me to be.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about things that you wouldn't normally feel that way about?

Oh, um... well... I really hate to complain, or make it sound like I'm not grateful for my family. I love them very much, I really do. But... yes, I suppose I have been feeling that way. 

It's just... we have a relative staying with us who needs some extra care, and it's been a bit of a disruption at home. I know I should be more patient, but lately I just... I keep telling myself I'm a terrible person because I feel so resentful about it all. I feel so ashamed even saying that out loud, please don't think I'm a monster. 

It's just that I keep replaying every impatient look I give, or every sharp comment I make, and it just feels like... like proof that I'm doing a horrible job. Sometimes I even think my husband and the rest of the family would just be better off without me dragging them down. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds incredibly dramatic, and I really don't want to be a burden to you or anyone else. Is that... is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I can try to explain it better if I'm not making sense.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual over the past month?

Oh, um... well, I don't think so? I mean, I know I said earlier that I feel like I'm dragging through mud because I'm so tired, but... I don't think I'm actually moving or talking any slower than normal. 

At least, I really hope I'm not. I try very hard to keep up my usual pace at the clinic so my coworkers don't have to pick up my slack, and no one has pointed out that I'm speaking differently. I think I'm still keeping up appearances in that regard. 

Is... is that okay? I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for, or if I'm misunderstanding the question. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate information I can.
Have you been having thoughts of death or dying frequently over the past month?

Oh, um... well... I really, really don't want to alarm you, and I know I shouldn't be thinking this way. I feel so guilty even bringing it up because I know I have so much to be thankful for. 

But... yes, I suppose I have been. It's actually... it's what finally scared me enough to make this appointment. I just... I keep having these thoughts that it would be so much easier if I just went to sleep and didn't wake up. Like everyone would just be relieved of the burden, you know? 

And... please don't think I'm crazy or that I'd actually do anything to hurt myself, I promise I'm trying so hard to keep it together. But sometimes, when I'm driving home from the clinic after a really long day, I'll just catch myself staring at the road and wondering... what would happen if I just didn't turn the wheel at the curve. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's probably terrible to hear, and I really don't want you to worry about me. I just... I wanted to be honest with you because I want to get better. Is it... is it normal to feel that way when things get this overwhelming? I hope I didn't say the wrong thing.
Have you experienced any feelings of hopelessness about the future over the past month?

Oh, um... I really hate to keep sounding so negative. I know I should be more optimistic, especially with my family around. I try so hard to keep a smile on my face for them. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... yes. It's just... most days lately, it feels like all the color has just drained out of everything. Even when the house is bustling and everyone is busy, I just feel this heavy, heavy emptiness. 

I don't want to bring anyone else down, so I usually try to hide it. Sometimes I'll just go into the laundry room and cry by myself because... well, I just can't stand the thought of them seeing how hopeless I really feel about things ever getting better. I feel so silly admitting that, hiding in a laundry room at my age. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm probably making it sound worse than it is, and I really am trying to look on the bright side. Is that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety over the past month?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I hope it's okay that I don't have that one. I know sometimes people get very antsy or pace around when they're overwhelmed, but... honestly, I just haven't had the energy to be restless. 

I've mostly just been feeling so heavy and still, like I mentioned before. When I'm at the clinic, I'm just focused on my work and keeping the animals calm, and when I'm home... well, I mostly just sit very quietly if I get a moment to myself. So, no, I wouldn't say I've been fidgety at all. 

Is... is that alright? I hope I'm not being unhelpful or difficult by saying no. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact right picture of what's going on, so you have everything you need.
Have you experienced any difficulty concentrating or making decisions over the past month?

Um... no, actually, I don't think so. I hope it's alright that I don't have that symptom either. I know I've been feeling so low, but my focus... it's actually been okay. 

At the clinic, I really have to stay sharp, you know, measuring out medications for the animals and assisting the vets, and I haven't had any trouble making decisions there. I really pride myself on not letting my work slip or burdening the rest of the team, even when I'm struggling so much inside. So I just push through and make sure everything is done exactly right. 

So... no, my concentration has been fine. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you the correct information.
Would you say your low mood and other symptoms have been present for most of the day, nearly every day, over the past month?

Oh, um... well, yes. It definitely has been there most of the day, nearly every day this past month. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, but... if I'm being perfectly honest, it's actually been going on for quite a while longer than that. 

I've been trying so hard to just manage it on my own, but... this heavy feeling, it's been hanging over me for about 11 months now. It's just that this past month, it's gotten so much harder to hide, and everything just feels... unbearable. I know I should have probably said something sooner, and I'm so sorry if I let it get out of hand before asking for help. I just really wanted to be strong for everyone. 

Is it... is it okay that it's been going on that long? I hope I'm not making things too complicated for you by bringing up the past year. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture like I'm supposed to.
Would you say that your symptoms have caused significant distress or impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of functioning over the past month?

Oh... um, well... yes. I suppose it has. I really, really hate to admit it because I try so hard not to be a burden on anyone, but... it has started affecting things. 

I know I just said I pride myself on not letting my work slip, but... if I'm being completely honest, I... I have started making a few mistakes at the clinic recently. Nothing that has hurt any of the animals! I promise, I would never let that happen. But just... little things. And I've been avoiding my friends, too. I just... I'm so afraid I'm either going to snap at them for no reason or just completely fall apart in front of them, and I don't want to ruin their day with my problems. 

And at home... oh, my poor husband. He's had to take over so much. He's doing the bills, making all the meals... and he's just... he's been having to keep such a close eye on me when my thoughts get really dark. I feel awful putting him through that. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible, and I really hope you don't think less of me for not holding it together better. I should be managing this. Is... is it okay that I'm struggling this much with my daily life? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Would you say that your symptoms have interfered with your ability to work or take care of things at home most days over the past month?

Um... yes, I think... I think I kind of just mentioned that, actually. I'm sorry, I hope I didn't jump ahead of you or mess up the order of your questions! I just get so nervous about making sure I tell you everything right. 

But, yes, to answer your question... it has been interfering most days. Like I was saying, I've... I've been making those little mistakes at the clinic, which I feel just terrible about. And I really have been pulling away from my friends, just because I don't want to burden them if I start crying or if I get irritable. 

And then at home... yes, my husband has really had to step up. I haven't been able to manage the bills or cook, and... and he's had to stay so close to me, just to make sure I'm safe when those really dark thoughts come up. I feel so guilty about all of it. I should be doing my part, you know? 

I hope it's okay that I kind of repeated myself there. Did that answer the question the way you needed me to?
Would you say that your low mood is mildly, moderately, or severely impairing your daily life?

Oh... um, well, I guess if I have to put a word on it... maybe severe? I really, really hate to use that word because it sounds so dramatic, and I promise I'm trying my best to push through it. I don't want to sound like I'm just giving up. 

But... like I was saying, with the mistakes at the clinic, and not seeing my friends because I'm so worried I'll ruin their mood by crying or snapping at them... and my poor husband having to do all the cooking and bills, plus watching over me when things get really bad... it just feels like it's taken over everything. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating the same things to you over and over. I hope I'm not frustrating you! Does... does "severe" sound like the right answer based on what I've told you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling irritable or restless to the point where you have trouble sitting still over the past month?

Oh... um, well... yes, a little bit, I suppose. I really hate to admit this part, because I know I sound awful, and I promise I'm usually a very patient person! I really try to be. But... earlier this month, I did have a few days where I felt just... almost electrically upbeat, I guess? Like I had all this energy humming inside me. 

But then... oh, it's so embarrassing to say. I ended up snapping at everyone over just... the tiniest little things. Like if someone misplaced a medication cup at the clinic, or if there was a sudden change in the morning schedule. I just got so unusually irritated, in a way that really didn't feel like my normal self at all. I felt terrible about it afterward, I really did. I apologized to everyone. 

I hope you don't think I'm just a difficult person to work with! I really do try to be easygoing. Is... is it normal to get that irritable sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm not sounding completely unreasonable.
Have you been feeling like you're fidgeting or have an inability to sit still when you're not working or actively doing something?

Um... yes, I think so. I really hope this doesn't make me sound frantic or, you know, out of control. I usually like to just relax in the evenings like a normal person! But... there were a few days recently where I just... I couldn't seem to just sit down and unwind after work. 

I feel a little silly even admitting this, but... I would just keep pacing around the house. I ended up pulling out a tape measure and measuring all the rooms, and I was making all these lists of things to do... and I even started completely reorganizing the kitchen cabinets. And I was doing all of this long after my husband had already gone to bed. 

I know it probably sounds a bit strange to be doing all that so late at night. I just had this nervous energy I couldn't shake. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of examples you're looking for.
Have you had any periods of at least two weeks where you felt better and your symptoms improved significantly over the past year?

Oh... um, no, not really. I'm so sorry, I wish I could give you a better answer, I really do. I know it must be frustrating to hear that I haven't been able to just... bounce back. I promise I've been trying to stay positive and keep my chin up! 

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to say this... this low feeling has just been kind of... hanging over me for a really long time. Like, maybe around 11 months now? It was there even before this past month got so... well, so unbearable. 

I really hate complaining, and I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it. I know I should probably be stronger than this. Does... does that make sense, that it could last that long? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way.
Would you describe your recent feelings of sadness and hopelessness as being most of the time or almost constantly present?

Oh... um, yes. I suppose so. I really hate to admit this, because I know I should be more positive, and I promise I really do try to put on a brave face for everyone! I don't want to drag my family down. But... if I'm answering honestly... yes, it's pretty much most days. 

It just feels like... well, like the color has completely drained out of everything. Even when the house is bustling and busy around me and things are perfectly fine, I just feel this heavy sadness. I feel so silly even saying this out loud, but... I actually end up going into the laundry room just to cry. I just can't stand the thought of anyone seeing how hopeless I feel right now. I don't want them to worry or think I'm falling apart. 

I hope it's okay that I'm sharing that with you? I know it's not a very cheerful answer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I can be a good patient for you.
